# Command-line reference

`kapto`: Records, visualises and selects robot data on the edge.

## Options for every command

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--config <FILE>` | Configuration file to use instead of the default location |
| `--server-bind <ADDRESS>` (or `--bind`) | Address the API and web UI listen on (`server.bind`) |
| `--server-port <PORT>` (or `--port`) | Port of the API and web UI (`server.port`) |
| `--viewer-stream-port <PORT>` | Port the viewer bridge streams poses and plotted values on (`viewer.stream_port`) |
| `--viewer-tap-socket <PATH>` | Unix socket live samples are sent to, for the viewer (`viewer.tap_socket`) |
| `--capture-control-socket <PATH>` | Unix socket the capture process takes its orders on (`capture.control_socket`) |
| `--paths-data <DIR>` (or `--data-dir`) | Where recordings and runtime state are stored (`paths.data`) |
| `--paths-packages <DIR>` (or `--packages-dir`) | Where robot packages are stored (`paths.packages`) |
| `--viewer-display-rate <HZ>` | How many times a second the live view moves the robot (`viewer.display_rate`) |
| `--viewer-history <MIB>` | MiB of recent live data the viewer bridge keeps for later viewers (`viewer.history`) |
| `--viewer-history-age <SECONDS>` | Seconds the live view can look back over (`viewer.history_age`) |
| `--viewer-stop-grace <SECONDS>` | Seconds the viewer bridge may take to stop before it is killed (`viewer.stop_grace`) |
| `--viewer-replay-cache-size <MIB>` | MiB replays of recorded episodes may take in the cache (`viewer.replay_cache_size`) |
| `--viewer-replay-cache-age <DAYS>` | Days unopened after which a replay leaves the cache (`viewer.replay_cache_age`) |
| `--capture-control-timeout <SECONDS>` | Seconds capture keeps recording after serve has gone (`capture.control_timeout`) |
| `--capture-stop-grace <SECONDS>` | Seconds the capture process may take to stop before it is killed (`capture.stop_grace`) |
| `--capture-disk-warn-below <MIB>` | MiB free below which Kapto warns the disk is running low (`capture.disk_warn_below`) |
| `--capture-disk-stop-below <MIB>` | MiB free below which recording stops and none starts (`capture.disk_stop_below`) |
| `--capture-pre-roll-max <MIB>` | The most MiB set aside for one stream's pre-roll (`capture.pre_roll_max`) |
| `--capture-preflight-window <SECONDS>` | Seconds pre-flight watches the streams (`capture.preflight_window`) |
| `--capture-preflight-disk-time <SECONDS>` | Seconds of recording pre-flight checks the disk has room for (`capture.preflight_disk_time`) |
| `--capture-preflight <POLICY>` | What a failed pre-flight check does to a start: refuse or warn (`capture.preflight`) |
| `--capture-attach-meshes <BOOL>` | Whether recordings also carry the robot package's meshes (`capture.attach_meshes`) |
| `--bin-keep-days <DAYS>` | Days an episode deleted by hand stays in the bin (`bin.keep_days`) |
| `--capture-compression <COMPRESSION>` | How recordings are compressed: lz4, zstd or none (`capture.compression`) |
| `--supervisor-restart-delay <SECONDS>` | Seconds before a process that exited is started again (`supervisor.restart_delay`) |
| `--supervisor-restart-max-delay <SECONDS>` | The longest wait before a process is started again (`supervisor.restart_max_delay`) |
| `--supervisor-stable-after <SECONDS>` | Seconds a process must run for its exit to count as a new failure (`supervisor.stable_after`) |
| `--worker-max-attempts <COUNT>` | How many times the worker may start a job (`worker.max_attempts`) |
| `--worker-pause-while-recording <BOOL>` | Whether the worker waits while an episode is recorded (`worker.pause_while_recording`) |
| `--upload-when <WHEN>` | Which episodes are uploaded by themselves (`upload.when`) |
| `--upload-pause-while-recording <BOOL>` | Whether uploads wait while an episode is recorded (`upload.pause_while_recording`) |
| `--upload-delete-local <WHEN>` | What happens to an episode's local copy once uploaded (`upload.delete_local`) |
| `--upload-min-verified-destinations <COUNT>` | On how many destinations an episode is verified before its local copy may go (`upload.min_verified_destinations`) |
| `--upload-verify <HOW>` | How uploaded files are checked (`upload.verify`) |
| `--upload-marker <BOOL>` | Whether the completeness marker is written (`upload.marker`) |
| `--upload-part-size <MIB>` | The size of a file's parts (`upload.part_size`) |
| `--upload-parallel-parts <COUNT>` | How many parts of a file go up at once (`upload.parallel_parts`) |
| `--upload-parallel-files <COUNT>` | How many files go up at once (`upload.parallel_files`) |
| `--upload-max-in-flight <COUNT>` | The most requests in flight at once (`upload.max_in_flight`) |
| `--upload-bandwidth <MIB_PER_S>` | The bandwidth cap; 0 for none (`upload.bandwidth`) |
| `--upload-max-attempts <COUNT>` | How many times a file is tried (`upload.max_attempts`) |
| `--upload-retry-failed-after <SECONDS>` | How long before a failed upload is tried again (`upload.retry_failed_after`) |
| `--upload-backoff-initial <SECONDS>` | The first wait before a request is tried again (`upload.backoff_initial`) |
| `--upload-backoff-max <SECONDS>` | The longest wait before a request is tried again (`upload.backoff_max`) |
| `--upload-timeout-connect <SECONDS>` | How long connecting may take (`upload.timeout_connect`) |
| `--upload-timeout-request <SECONDS>` | How long one request may take (`upload.timeout_request`) |
| `--viewer-camera-max-fps <HZ>` | Frames a second, at most, of each camera sent to the live view (`viewer.camera_max_fps`) |
| `--viewer-camera-history <MIB>` | MiB of every camera's pictures the viewer bridge keeps to look back over (`viewer.camera_history`) |
| `--viewer-camera-history-fps <HZ>` | Pictures a second of each camera the viewer bridge keeps to look back over (`viewer.camera_history_fps`) |
| `--viewer-camera-history-width <PIXELS>` | Pixels wide, at most, the pictures the viewer bridge keeps to look back over are (`viewer.camera_history_width`) |
| `--viewer-frame-socket <PATH>` | Unix socket cameras' frames are sent to, for the viewer (`viewer.frame_socket`) |
| `-h`, `--help` | Print help |
| `-V`, `--version` | Print the version (top level only) |

## `kapto config`

Inspect Kapto's configuration.

## `kapto config validate`

Check the configuration and report every problem.

## `kapto config show`

Show every setting with its value and where the value came from.

## `kapto record`

Record one episode from the UDP streams declared in a streams.toml, for a fixed time, into the data directory.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--streams <FILE>` | The streams.toml declaring each stream's UDP port and rate |
| `--mapping <FILE>` | The mapping.toml saying which decoded value drives which joint, carried by each recording when the streams aren't declared in a robot package, so its quality checks know the joints |
| `--duration <SECONDS>` | How long to record, in seconds |

## `kapto capture`

Receive every stream declared in a streams.toml for as long as it runs, feeding the live view, and record episodes when told to over the control socket; SIGINT or SIGTERM finalises the episode being recorded and stops.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--streams <FILE>` | The streams.toml declaring each stream's input and rate |
| `--mapping <FILE>` | The mapping.toml saying which decoded value drives which joint, carried by each recording when the streams aren't declared in a robot package, so its quality checks know the joints |

## `kapto episode`

Start and stop episodes of a running `kapto capture`, or show what it is doing.

## `kapto episode start`

Start recording an episode.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--duration <SECONDS>` | Stop by itself after this many seconds; without it, records until `kapto episode stop` |
| `--profile <ID>` | Record it with this session profile from the configuration folder (`kapto profile list`), for the robot package capture records; a copy is kept in the episode |
| `--task <ID>` | Record it for this task from the configuration folder (`kapto task list`); a copy is kept in the episode |
| `--waive <CODE>` | Record even though this pre-flight check failed, given by its cause code (e.g. `preflight.stream_silent`); repeat for each. The episode says which checks were waived |

## `kapto episode stop`

Stop recording, and wait until the episode is finalised.

## `kapto episode abort`

Stop recording and discard the episode: nothing of it is kept.

## `kapto episode status`

Show whether an episode is being recorded, and each stream's counts.

## `kapto episode preflight`

Check again, between episodes, that this machine can record what the robot sends: room and speed of the disk, each stream at its declared rate. Fails if a check fails.

## `kapto episode event`

Send an event: something that happened now, or the beginning, end or whole of a stretch. Recorded in the episode being recorded; between episodes only told to whoever watches.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--kind <KIND>` | Its kind, from the event vocabulary: `events.toml` in the configuration folder (or `note`, `problem` and `intervention` without it), and each task's subtasks as `subtask.<name>` |
| `--begin <ID>` | It begins a stretch, paired with its end by this ID |
| `--end <ID>` | It ends the stretch begun with this ID |
| `--last <SECONDS>` | It is a whole stretch: the last this many seconds, ending now |
| `--text <TEXT>` | What to say about it |

## `kapto episode delete`

Delete a finalised episode: it goes into the bin, as it is, until the bin is emptied (after `bin.keep_days`), and can be put back until then. Needs `kapto serve` running.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| ` <EPISODE>` | The episode's ID, as `kapto` lists it |

## `kapto episode restore`

Put an episode deleted by hand back from the bin, as it was. Needs `kapto serve` running.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| ` <EPISODE>` | The episode's ID |

## `kapto package`

List the robot packages Kapto finds, or show one: what identifies it and its files.

## `kapto package list`

List the robot packages in the packages folder (`paths.packages`): each one's ID, version and content hash.

## `kapto package show`

Show one robot package: what its package.toml says, its files and its content hash.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| ` <PACKAGE>` | A package folder, or the ID of a package in the packages folder |

## `kapto package import`

Make a robot package from a robot description found elsewhere, such as a vendor's repository: the URDF and every mesh and texture it names, copied into a new package in the packages folder so each is found as the URDF names it, with a package.toml, a streams.toml to fill in and a mapping.toml listing each moving joint.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| ` <URDF>` | The robot's URDF |
| `--id <ID>` | The new package's ID, which is also its folder's name |
| `--name <NAME>` | What people call the robot; the URDF's robot name if not given |
| `--arg <NAME:=VALUE>` | An argument of a xacro description, `name:=value`, as ROS's xacro takes it; repeat for each |

## `kapto package lint`

Check a robot package: its files, the robot description and meshes, the streams and the mapping, reporting every problem with where it is and what to do. Fails if there are errors; warnings don't.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| ` <PACKAGE>` | A package folder, or the ID of a package in the packages folder |
| `--format <FORMAT>` | text for people, json for tools |

## `kapto profile`

List the session profiles in the configuration folder, or show one: with which robot, by whom, where and how episodes are recorded.

## `kapto profile list`

List the profiles in the configuration folder: each one's ID, robot package, mode and operator.

## `kapto profile show`

Show one profile: everything it says.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| ` <PROFILE>` | The profile's ID: its file's name without .toml |

## `kapto task`

List the tasks in the configuration folder, or show one: what the robot is asked to do.

## `kapto task list`

List the tasks in the configuration folder: each one's ID, name and number of subtasks.

## `kapto task show`

Show one task: everything it says.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| ` <TASK>` | The task's ID: its file's name without .toml |

## `kapto decode`

Show a recording's messages as named values, decoded with the layouts stored in it; streams without one are shown as raw bytes. With --pcap and --package, decode a packet capture with a package's streams.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| ` <PATH>` | An episode folder, or its recording.mcap |
| `--pcap <FILE>` | A packet capture (pcap or pcapng, e.g. from `tcpdump -w`) to decode instead, with the streams of --package |
| `--package <PACKAGE>` | The robot package whose streams.toml says which UDP port each stream arrives on and how to decode it: a folder, or a package ID |
| `--stream <NAME>` | Only this stream; repeat for several. Every stream if left out |
| `--format <FORMAT>` | table: the first messages of each stream; csv: every message of one stream |
| `--limit <MESSAGES>` | Messages per stream. The table shows 10 unless told otherwise; CSV writes every message |

## `kapto demo`

Try Kapto without a robot: run it with the built-in sample arm and a synthetic robot sending its joint states, then open the address it prints.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--robot-port <PORT>` | UDP port the synthetic robot sends to and Kapto receives on |
| `--rate <HZ>` | Messages per second the synthetic robot sends |
| `--no-camera` | Leave out the synthetic wrist camera, whose pictures (640x480 JPEG, 30 a second) Kapto receives over TCP on the port after the robot's |

## `kapto showcase`

Show Kapto to people in one command: the demo, narrated step by step, recording ordinary episodes and then one in which the robot misbehaves, and saying what Kapto found and where to watch it.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--unattended` | Run every step on by itself instead of waiting for Enter |
| `--episodes <N>` | Ordinary episodes recorded before the robot misbehaves: what the anomaly model learns from (3 or more) |
| `--seconds <SECONDS>` | Seconds each ordinary episode lasts |
| `--robot-port <PORT>` | UDP port the synthetic robot sends to and Kapto receives on |

## `kapto serve`

Run Kapto: start the capture process, the viewer bridge and the worker, keep them running, serve the API, and stop everything on SIGINT or SIGTERM.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--robot <FILE>` | The robot's URDF file |
| `--streams <FILE>` | The streams.toml declaring each stream's input and rate |
| `--mapping <FILE>` | The mapping.toml saying which decoded value drives which joint |

## `kapto viz-bridge`

Stream the robot moving live to the web UI's live view, from the samples a running capture process or recording sends; runs until interrupted.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--robot <FILE>` | The robot's URDF file |
| `--streams <FILE>` | The streams.toml the recording uses |
| `--mapping <FILE>` | The mapping.toml saying which decoded value drives which joint |
| `--duration <SECONDS>` | Stop after this many seconds; without it, runs until interrupted |
| `--parent <PID>` | End when process PID ends, even if it is killed: serve passes its own, so this ends with it |

## `kapto worker`

Do the jobs `kapto serve` queues, such as checking each finalised episode's files against its manifest, one at a time; runs until SIGINT or SIGTERM. Serve starts it.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--parent <PID>` | End when process PID ends, even if it is killed: serve passes its own, so this ends with it |

## `kapto topics`

List the ROS 2 topics this machine's ROS 2 network has, with their message types, for declaring a ROS 2 robot's streams. Only the Kapto of the `kapto-ros2` image is built with ROS 2.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| `--wait <SECONDS>` | Seconds to wait for publishers to announce themselves before listing their topics |
| `--streams` | Print each topic as a `streams.toml` declaration, with the rate it published at while Kapto listened (another --wait seconds), and the largest message seen where that is larger than the default |

## `kapto export`

Write an episode in another tool's format: its ROS 2 topics as a rosbag2 bag that `ros2 bag play` plays back on the robot's topics.

## `kapto export rosbag2`

Write the episode's ROS 2 topics as a rosbag2 bag (one MCAP file), each on the topic it was recorded from, with both timestamps as recorded, for `ros2 bag play <file>`; Kapto's own channels and other streams are left out.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| ` <EPISODE>` | The episode folder, or its recording.mcap |
| `--output <FILE>` | The bag to write, e.g. episode.mcap; never overwritten |

## `kapto upload`

Work with the upload destinations in `[[upload.destination]]`: test that each can be written to as an upload would.

## `kapto upload check`

Test each upload destination, or the one named, as an upload would use it: write a small probe object under its prefix, read it back and remove it. Fails if any can't be written or read.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| ` <DESTINATION>` | The destination's `name`; every destination if left out |

## `kapto upload status`

Show where uploads are: each destination's episodes uploaded, uploading and failed, and each upload not done.

## `kapto upload retry`

Try an episode's failed uploads again now, without waiting for `upload.retry_failed_after`. Needs `kapto serve` running.

| Option | Description |
|---|---|
| ` <EPISODE>` | The episode's ID |
